title: Designing CLI Error Messages: A Practical Guide
angle: Most guides say "be human-friendly"; this one gives senior engineers building internal tools a concrete what→why→fix template, stdout/stderr/exit-code/color rules that survive scripts and CI, and internal-tool remediation such as runbook links and exact auth commands.
description: Design CLI error messages people can act on: what→why→fix structure, stderr vs stdout, exit codes, NO_COLOR, and remediation for internal tools.
excerpt: A good CLI error tells you what happened, why, and what to do next, and it still works in pipes and CI. Here is a practical pattern for senior engineers building internal tools.

outline.heading: What makes a CLI error message good?
points: Open with the claim: an error is the moment your tool is read most carefully, so treat it as UI.
Define the standard: what happened, why, how to fix it, plus optional error code and docs URL.
Show a bad vs good before/after example.

facts.fact: The main trend across sources is structured errors that hold up in scripts and CI: what happened, why, how to fix it, plus an optional error code and docs URL.
clig.dev example: "Can't write to file.txt. You might need to make it writable by running 'chmod +w file.txt'."

outline.heading: Catch expected errors and rewrite them for humans
points: Never show raw stack traces for expected failures such as bad input, missing files or permissions.
Include specifics: file paths, values, constraints.
Show a catch-at-the-top pattern that maps known exceptions to messages.

facts.fact: clig.dev says to rewrite expected errors for humans.

outline.heading: Keep signal high: grouping, ordering and restraint
points: Group repeated errors under one explanatory header instead of near-identical lines.
Put the most important information at the end, where the eye lands.
Skip ERR/WARN labels in human output; reserve them for verbose mode.
Use red sparingly.

facts.fact: clig.dev says signal-to-noise ratio is crucial.

outline.heading: Send errors to stderr and get exit codes right
points: Errors, warnings and logs go to stderr; stdout stays for data so pipes are not polluted.
Exit 0 on success and non-zero on failure.
Address the disagreement openly: 0/1 by default vs a few mapped codes. Recommend a small documented set only when scripts need to branch (retry, skip, alert).
Document codes in --help or the man page.

facts.fact: clig.dev: exit 0 on success, non-zero on failure, with distinct codes mapped to important failure modes; send errors to stderr.
Better CLI and other sources say to use 0/1 unless there is a strong reason for more, and to document any codes.

outline.heading: Color and formatting that don't break logs and CI
points: Disable color when the stream is not a TTY, NO_COLOR is set, TERM=dumb, or --no-color is passed.
Explain NO_COLOR scope: color only, not bold/underline; user config or flags may override.
Warn against over-coloring.

facts.fact: NO_COLOR: if the env var is present and non-empty, don't emit ANSI color, whatever its value. It covers color only, and is supported by hundreds of libraries and tools.
clig.dev color rules: disable when not a TTY, NO_COLOR set, TERM=dumb, or --no-color passed.

outline.heading: Handle unexpected errors: debug output and bug reports
points: Keep debug output behind -v, -d or --debug rather than dumping it by default.
For crashes, write a detailed log to a file instead of flooding the terminal.
Give a bug-report path, ideally a pre-populated issue URL with system info.

facts.fact: For unexpected errors, print debug context and traceback or write a log file, and give bug-report instructions, ideally a pre-populated issue URL with system info.

outline.heading: Error messages for internal tools: point at your own runbook
points: Add team-specific remediation: runbook link, owning channel, the exact login or auth command.
Use stable error codes plus docs URLs so support can search for them.
Flag this as a recommendation from experience, not a standard.

outline.heading: Checklist: ship-ready CLI error messages
points: Short scannable checklist covering what/why/fix, stderr, exit code, color rules, grouping, debug flag, bug-report path.

gaps: Concrete before/after rewrites, where competitors give only principles
stdout vs stderr, exit code and NO_COLOR/TTY rules in one place, and the exit-code granularity disagreement
Internal-tool remediation (runbooks, owning channel, exact auth command)
Unexpected-error handling: log file plus pre-populated bug-report URL
